articles.title: India to Cut Visa Form Fields by Around 70% in Overhaul for Foreign Travellers
articles.excerpt: The Home Ministry plans slimmer forms across all 22 visa categories from next year, dropping the 'district' field and letting tourists list a hotel as their local address.
articles.nri_angle: Simpler Indian visa paperwork for foreign-national relatives, spouses and friends of the diaspora planning trips to India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Survey: Most Microsoft India Staff Report Hikes Of Five Percent Or Less
articles.excerpt: A Blind survey of 2,178 India-based professionals found 91% of Microsoft respondents reporting hikes of 5% or less — self-reported figures that arrive alongside a voluntary buyout offer to about 60,000 employees.
articles.image_caption: An aerial view shows Microsoft's West Campus in Redmond, Washington. A Blind survey found 91% of Microsoft India respondents received pay hikes of 5% or less this year.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian tech workers in India and the diaspora, the survey captures pay anxiety arriving at the same time as a large voluntary exit offer at one of the sector's biggest employers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK Doubles Settlement Wait to Ten Years, Keeps Five-Year Route for Care Workers
articles.excerpt: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's earned-settlement plan doubles the standard ILR wait from five years to ten, applied retrospectively — but care workers earning at least £25,000 who met their visa conditions, higher earners, and many public sector workers keep a five-year route.
articles.image_caption: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood leaves 10 Downing Street in London. The government plans to double the qualifying wait for permanent settlement to ten years, while care workers keep a five-year route if they meet visa and earnings conditions.
articles.nri_angle: Indians are one of the largest groups on UK work and health and care visas, so the doubled ten-year default — and the care-worker and salary carve-outs — directly change settlement timelines for thousands of Indian families in Britain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICE Officer Indicted in Houston Had Been on Job Just Over a Year
articles.excerpt: Mario Alberto Morales, a 2025 surge hire, surrendered Monday on an aggravated-assault indictment over an October 10 vehicle strike in Houston. He denies wrongdoing, ICE calls the case a political stunt — and his hiring record is now part of the story.
articles.nri_angle: The case tests how the rapid expansion of ICE's workforce is vetted and trained — a question with direct consequences for immigrant communities, including Indian nationals, facing enforcement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Officer Morales indicted on October 10 incident.
Victim Miguel Parra Hernandez suffered multiple leg fractures.
Next court hearing scheduled for December 2.

articles.title: 'The Boat's Sunk': Kansas City Immigration Court Buried Under 40,000 Cases
articles.excerpt: Attorneys in Kansas City warn that the only immigration court serving Missouri and Kansas is overwhelmed by a backlog KMBC puts at about 40,000 cases — with too few judges and too few lawyers for the people waiting on hearings.

sources.label: US Department of Justice, EOIR — Kansas City Immigration Court

articles.nri_angle: Indian and other immigrant families in Missouri and Kansas wait in this single court's queue for asylum and removal decisions, often without a lawyer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 66 Lawmakers Urge Trump Administration to Halt Afghan Deportation Flights
articles.excerpt: A bicameral letter led by Rep. Scott Peters asks Secretaries Rubio and Mullin to cancel flights that would send at least 150 Afghans from Louisiana to Pakistan — with Afghanistan, an ICE officer's court declaration says, the intended final destination.
articles.nri_angle: South Asian readers with Afghan family, colleagues or community ties face a live removal operation this week; the congressional letter is the main public challenge to it so far.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Afghans planned for deportation through Pakistan

articles.title: Tennessee DACA Recipients Sue Over Driver's Licenses Denied Under New Law
articles.excerpt: A law that took effect October 1 requires a federally authorized period of stay for a temporary license — a test DACA recipients and some work-permit holders no longer pass. Advocates sued on October 30 to block it.
articles.nri_angle: Indian and other immigrant residents of Tennessee on work permits should check whether their temporary license renewal is affected before it expires.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indiaspora Warns Targeting H-1B Holders Poses 'Very Serious' Risk to US Economy
articles.excerpt: The diaspora organisation's October 30 statement flagged five proposed curbs — and urged US leaders to reject anti-Indian rhetoric ahead of the midterms.
articles.image_caption: Letter tiles spell out 'H-1B Visa' over a US flag. Indiaspora warned that targeting H-1B holders could have serious economic consequences for communities across the United States.
articles.nri_angle: With Indians taking 71% of approved H-1Bs, the curbs Indiaspora lists would land almost entirely on Indian professionals, students and spouses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada Reminds International Students: You Can Work Only If Your Study Permit Says So
articles.excerpt: IRCC's fresh warning: the permission is printed on the permit itself, off-campus work is capped at 24 hours a week in session, and breaching the conditions can cost a student their status.
articles.nri_angle: Indians form one of the largest international student cohorts in Canada, and unauthorised work is among the most common ways their status is put at risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: H-1B Visas and Green Cards After the Midterms: What Indian Professionals Should Watch
articles.excerpt: The November 3 elections will not change anyone's visa status overnight. What they decide is which of three live bills — on H-1B salary thresholds, a proposed issuance pause, and a points-based green card system — gets a Congress willing to move it.
articles.nri_angle: Indians account for more than 70% of H-1B approvals and face the longest employment-based green card waits, so the bills below matter to them first.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Texas Agriculture Department Bars H-1B Employers From Its State Grants
articles.excerpt: Commissioner Sid Miller's October 28 policy cuts businesses employing H-1B workers out of Texas Department of Agriculture grants and challenges other state officials to follow.

sources.label: Texas Department of Agriculture announcement (via EIN Presswire)

articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals are the largest H-1B group in Texas; employers who hire them now risk losing state agriculture grant eligibility.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: In Texas's Rio Grande Valley, the Deportation Drive Is Galvanising the Midterm Vote
articles.excerpt: The Valley swung to Trump in 2024 over the border. Two years of domestic enforcement — a $180.6 million hit to the local economy, an ACLU poll showing 63 percent say ICE has gone too far, and deportations like a Progreso woman's within 36 hours of a hearing — are swinging it back days before the November 3 midterms.
articles.nri_angle: The Valley's story is the national one for immigrant communities, including Indian families in Texas: enforcement has shifted from the border to workplaces, hearings and missed court dates inside the country, and the November 3 result will shape funding and oversight of that machinery.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nearly 1 Million Indians in Green Card Backlog Face Fresh H-1B Scrutiny
articles.excerpt: A proposal to end deference to earlier H-1B approvals could bring more evidence requests and delays for Indian professionals who, by one estimate, could wait up to 179 years for an employment-based green card.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals in the backlog could face more RFEs and delays at H-1B extension, risking the 240-day work-authorisation window.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Australia Visa Biometrics Start for India: Five Checks Before You Book

articles.title: Immigration Roundup: India's EB-3 Date Advances, New Zealand Widens Business Visas
articles.excerpt: The November 2026 Visa Bulletin moves India's EB-3 final action date three weeks while EB-2 stays frozen at November 2013, and New Zealand broadens business visitor and specialist work pathways effective October 20.
articles.image_caption: An Indian passport. India's EB-3 priority date advanced in the latest round of immigration changes covered in the roundup.

sources.label: U.S. Department of State — Visa Bulletin for November 2026
Murthy Law Firm — November 2026 Visa Bulletin

articles.nri_angle: Indian green card applicants can check November I-485 filing eligibility against the January 15, 2015 Dates for Filing cutoff for EB-2 and EB-3 India, while Indian business travellers gain wider permitted activities in New Zealand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian National Convicted of Voting Illegally in 2024 US Presidential Election
articles.excerpt: A federal jury in Fort Worth convicted Khalwinder Singh Bhengura, a green card holder from India, of voting by an alien and falsely claiming US citizenship to register. Sentencing is set for February 11, 2027.
articles.image_caption: A US ballot box (file photo). An Indian national was convicted of voting illegally in the 2024 US presidential election.
articles.nri_angle: For green card holders: voting in a federal election — or even registering by claiming citizenship — can mean prison, fines and removal from the US, even before naturalization is complete.

articles.excerpt: The removed filing sought a financial analyst at about $65,000 starting February 2027, weeks after Florida's pause on new university H-1B hires expires.
articles.nri_angle: Florida's pause on new university H-1B hires affects Indian academics and staff seeking US university jobs, while existing holders can still renew.

articles.title: Infosys CEO Says US Immigration Curbs Will Not Raise Costs or Attrition
articles.excerpt: Salil Parekh told investors a majority-local US workforce insulates Infosys from the PERM suspension and H-1B pressure, even as individual green-card cases face delays.
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT workers in the US face delayed green-card filings under the PERM suspension even though Infosys says its business and costs are unaffected.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Proposed $70,000 OPT Fee Would Sharply Raise Cost of Student Work Permits
articles.excerpt: A Department of Homeland Security proposal would charge schools $70,000 for a first OPT recommendation and $30,000 for each later one, including STEM extensions — up from about $500 today — with public comments open through November 9.
articles.image_caption: An academic procession at the University of Washington (file photo, Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian students are one of the largest international cohorts in the US and heavily represented in STEM programmes, so a $70,000 OPT recommendation fee would directly reprice the F-1-to-first-job route many Indian graduates rely on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.card_title: Projected Financial Impact of OPT Fees

articles.title: Republican Bill Would Raise H-1B Exemption Threshold to Nearly $140,000
articles.excerpt: House and Senate versions of the Protecting American Workers Through H-1B Modernization Act would replace the $60,000 salary exemption for H-1B-dependent employers, frozen since 1998, with twice the national average wage index — nearly $140,000 today.
articles.image_caption: The US House of Representatives chamber, where the H-1B exemption bill sits in committee (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals receive the bulk of H-1B visas and Indian and Indian-origin IT services firms are among the employers most likely to be classed H-1B-dependent, so a higher exemption threshold would fall hardest on the hiring model many Indian professionals enter through.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
